candidates.change_summary: Replace the require statement with a condition allowing anyone to withdraw
Replace the transfer recipient with msg.sender instead of Owner
Delete the transfer statement so withdraw does nothing
Replace the require condition with a trivially false one, permanently blocking withdrawals
Remove the require statement that checks msg.sender == Owner, allowing anyone to call Command.
Remove the low-level call, making Command a no-op that returns success but does nothing.

Replace `(address(this).balance + msg.value) >= address(this).balance` with `(address(this).balance + msg.value) >= address(this).balance + 1` so the require condition can fail when the invariant holds, changing the execution path.

Replace `payable(adr).transfer(address(this).balance+msg.value)` with `payable(adr).transfer(address(this).balance)` so the transferred amount is smaller, causing `multiplicate` to leave a different contract balance.

Replace `address(this).balance+msg.value` in the transfer with `msg.value` so only the sent value is transferred, not the whole balance plus sent value, leaving the contract with a non-zero balance after the call.
Replace `if(msg.value>=address(this).balance)` with `if(msg.value>address(this).balance)` so the condition is stricter, preventing the transfer when msg.value equals the balance.
Delete the require statement so the overflow check is skipped, allowing the transfer to proceed even if the invariant is violated, potentially changing the balance outcome.
